samples.summary: No test that a character-reference quote breakout in an attribute value cannot escape the attribute
samples.evidence: The only escaping test (`escapes the alt text rather than emitting it as markup`, line ~63) feeds `alt="<b> & more"`. `parseAttrs` runs every value (including `src`) through `md.utils.unescapeAll`, which resolves `"`/`"` into a literal `"` before the value is handed to the renderer. The sharpest case for the plugin's security claim — e.g. `` or `` — is never rendered in any test, so nothing in the suite would fail if the output escaping the plugin relies on stopped covering quotes. Searched img-plugin.test.ts for `"`/`&#`/`unescapeAll`/`normalizeLink` (no matches) and grepped preview.test.ts for `img`/`alt=` (only the two new wiring tests).

samples.summary: The documented "alt is literal, not markdown" behavior has no test
samples.evidence: imgRule deliberately pushes the alt text as a single `text` child instead of running it through the inline parser (comment at img-plugin.ts:157-160). No test in img-plugin.test.ts renders an alt containing markdown syntax (e.g. `alt="*em* [x](y) `c`"`), so if that child were ever built via `md.inline.parse`, or if `token.content` were used alone, the suite would still be green for markup-bearing alts. The nearest test only checks HTML character references, not markdown constructs.
searchedFor: grep for '*' / backtick alt cases in img-plugin.test.ts

samples.summary: parseAttrs' stray-text rejection branches (lines 84 and 108) are not exercised by any refused case
samples.evidence: The code explicitly documents refusing regions with "a stray quote or `=`" (line 82-84) and trailing junk (line 108). Walking the refused list in img-plugin.test.ts (lines 95-112), every entry is rejected earlier: unknown name, duplicate name, missing value, bad dimension, empty/absent src, validateLink. No input such as ``, `` or `` appears, so both null-returns are untested and a regression there (accepting a malformed tag) would ship undetected.

samples.summary: Two refused-list cases pass regardless of the plugin's behavior
samples.evidence: `['another tag entirely', '<video src="a.mp4">']` and `['a stray closing tag', '</img>']` assert only `not.toContain('<img')` and `toContain('<')`. With `html: false`, both hold whether or not imgPlugin is registered at all (no `<img` could appear from `<video>`, and `</img>` never reaches the rule body via `startsImgTag`'s `<img` prefix check plus `IMG_TAG_RE`'s `^<img` anchor). They document intent but cannot fail on any plausible plugin regression.

samples.summary: Accepted-dimension matrix is partial: no percentage height and no height-only tag
samples.evidence: DIMENSION_RE (`/^\d+%?$/`) is applied to both width and height, but the tests only cover `width=50%` (percent) and `height="20"` (digits). No test renders `height="50%"` or a tag with height but no width, so an asymmetric bug in the height branch (img-plugin.ts:141/156) would be invisible.
searchedFor: read all accepted-case tests in img-plugin.test.ts

samples.summary: startsImgTag's end-of-input (NaN charCodeAt) path has no test
samples.evidence: The comment at img-plugin.ts:113-119 justifies `charCodeAt` past the end returning NaN. No test renders a truncated prefix such as `<im`, `<i`, or a bare `<` at end of line, so the boundary the comment defends is unexercised (the `does not swallow the rest of the line` test uses a full `<img` prefix).
searchedFor: read img-plugin.test.ts fully for '<im' / bare '<' inputs
